zh.title: 以后最好的广告，可能不是一张图，而是一个会聊天的销售
zh.excerpt: 当广告开始听懂空间、预算、偏好和顾虑，成交不再只靠一句口号。新的机会，是把产品知识变成一场诚实的对话。
zh.content:
![以后最好的广告，可能不是一张图，而是一个会聊天的销售](/assets/notes/2026-09-24-conversational-ads/cover.png)

假设你正准备买一把椅子。

广告告诉你：**限时优惠、设计大奖、今天下单立减300元。**

但你真正想问的是：

“我家只有30平方米，它会不会太大？”

“家里有一只猫，这种面料好不好打理？”

“我的腰不太舒服，坐久了会不会累？”

“门只有75厘米宽，搬得进去吗？”

一张广告图回答不了这些问题。落地页可能写了几十屏，你也未必愿意自己翻。

如果广告旁边坐着一个懂产品、不会催单、甚至愿意告诉你“这款不适合你”的人，事情就不一样了。

这正是我看到 **Sponsored Agents** 时，最感兴趣的地方。

它改变的也许不是广告长什么样，而是广告第一次可以认真听完一个人的问题。

![广告从一张海报，变成一段能听懂真实问题的对话](/assets/notes/2026-09-24-conversational-ads/shift.png)

## 01｜广告第一次从“一句话”，变成“一段对话”

9月16日，OpenAI公布了 ChatGPT Ads 的一系列新能力，其中包括正在测试的 Sponsored Agents。

用户看到一条明确标注的广告后，可以主动进入与品牌智能体的对话。他可以继续追问自己的空间、预算、偏好和顾虑，了解产品是否真的适合自己，再决定要不要前往品牌网站。

OpenAI举的例子就是一张餐桌。

看到餐桌只是开始。用户还会问：它能坐几个人？放不放得进我的餐厅？应该怎么保养？

过去，广告负责把人带到网页，网页负责把所有信息一股脑摆出来。

现在，中间多了一层：**先把这个人的真实问题问清楚。**

9月23日，ChatGPT Ads 又开始向印度尼西亚、马来西亚、菲律宾、新加坡、泰国、越南和台湾扩展。OpenAI称它已覆盖60多个国家和地区。

这不代表 Sponsored Agents 已经在所有市场开放。它目前仍只面向美国部分广告主测试。但方向已经很明显：

> **广告正在从“请看我”，变成“你想知道什么？”**

## 02｜真正好的销售，不是更会说，而是更会判断

传统广告最擅长回答一个问题：

**“为什么你应该买我？”**

对话式广告必须回答另一个更难的问题：

**“在你的具体情况里，我到底适不适合你？”**

这两句话看起来只差一点，背后的逻辑完全不同。

前者要放大优点，后者要理解限制。前者追求点击，后者需要信任。

一个真正有用的品牌智能体，不能只背诵宣传语。它要知道产品的尺寸、价格、材质、交付时间、售后边界，也要知道哪些需求它解决不了。

有时候，它最有价值的一句话可能是：

**“如果你最在意的是这个，我不建议你买这一款。”**

短期看，这句话少了一笔订单。长期看，它可能第一次让用户相信：屏幕对面不是一个只想成交的机器。

## 03｜落地页不会消失，它的工作变了

很多人看到对话式广告，会自然想到：以后是不是不需要官网、不需要详情页，也不需要设计了？

我的判断正好相反。

当AI替用户总结产品，品牌自己的内容会变成AI回答问题的依据。产品参数写得含糊、案例是假的、不同页面互相矛盾，智能体只会更快暴露这些问题。

未来几层内容的分工会更清楚：

- **广告负责相遇：** 在用户产生需求时出现。
- **对话负责判断：** 问清场景、顾虑与限制。
- **官网负责证明：** 展示真实案例、细节、价格和品牌态度。
- **App负责体验：** 让承诺真正发生，并形成长期关系。
- **产品负责兑现：** 最终价值仍由产品本身完成。

AI没有让品牌变得不重要。它让含糊的品牌更难躲过去，也让认真做产品的人更容易被理解。

## 04｜如果换成我自己的产品

假设有人看到一休的介绍，不再只看见一句“帮助你放松”，而是可以先问：

“我经常凌晨三点醒来，不想听人声，只想听十分钟自然声，有适合的吗？”

一个好的回答不应该夸大疗效。它可以说明一休提供什么、不能替代什么，再根据时间和声音偏好，推荐晨林鸟语或另一段声音，让用户先试听。

如果是三慢问道，用户可能问：

“我最近在工作上很纠结，《道德经》对这种状态能给我什么启发？”

智能体不必假装替人做决定。它可以介绍“原文、解释、对我们的启发、生活中的道”这条阅读路径，让对方判断这是不是自己愿意每天读一点的方式。

如果是虾子曰，用户也许会说：

“我做跨境电商，只想知道昨天值得关注的AI和消费品牌变化，还想打开英文原文。”

这时，对话的价值不是把18张海报再复述一遍，而是帮助他快速找到与自己有关的部分。

这些场景目前只是我的产品设计推演，并非已经上线的广告或智能体功能。但它让我更清楚一件事：

> **产品介绍不该只讲“我有什么”，还应该帮助用户判断“这和我有什么关系”。**

![一人公司把真实产品知识，变成可以持续回答问题的销售能力](/assets/notes/2026-09-24-conversational-ads/knowledge.png)

## 05｜这是一人公司被低估的机会

过去，只有大公司养得起覆盖多个时区、熟悉全部产品、还能讲多种语言的售前团队。

一人公司通常只能写一个FAQ，再祈祷用户愿意看完。

对话式销售给小团队提供了另一种可能：

- 用户凌晨提问，也能得到基于真实资料的回答；
- 同一个产品，可以用不同语言解释给不同市场；
- 那些不会主动私信的问题，也有机会被听见；
- 每一次提问，都会反过来告诉创作者：用户真正犹豫的是什么。

但这里没有“接上AI就会自动成交”的魔法。

AI销售的上限，取决于你给它的产品事实；它的下限，则取决于你愿不愿意承认产品边界。

对一人公司来说，真正需要建设的不是一套更油滑的话术，而是一座可以被持续维护的**产品知识库**：真实参数、使用场景、适合谁、不适合谁、常见问题、比较依据、交付流程和售后规则。

## 06｜现在就可以做的5件事

1. **收集30个真实问题。** 从私信、评论、客服和朋友试用里找，不要坐在办公室里想象。
2. **专门写一页“不适合谁”。** 一个敢于拒绝错误订单的产品，更容易获得正确用户的信任。
3. **把证明放回自己的官网。** 案例、价格、参数和更新记录要能被找到，也能被引用。
4. **先把中文说清楚，再做多语言。** 翻译可以交给AI，模糊的产品定位无法靠翻译补救。
5. **记录问题，不只记录点击。** 用户反复追问的地方，往往就是产品下一次应该改进的地方。

## 07｜广告最终还是一面镜子

我一直不太喜欢那种追着人跑的广告。

它知道我点过什么，却不知道我为什么犹豫；它不断催我下单，却从不问这个东西是否真的适合我。

对话式广告至少提供了另一种可能：品牌不再只占用几秒注意力，而是在用户愿意的时候，认真回答一个具体问题。

当然，它也会把坏产品的缺点放大得更快。

如果产品没有价值，智能体只是一个更勤快的推销员；如果资料不真实，它只会更流畅地说错话。

所以，下一代广告真正竞争的也许不是谁的模型更聪明，而是：

**谁更了解自己的产品，谁更尊重用户的问题，谁愿意用一次诚实的回答，换一段更长久的关系。**

以后最好的广告，可能真的不是一张图。

它更像一个懂产品、有分寸、不会缠着你下单的人。

当你需要的时候，它刚好坐在那里。

---

事实说明：OpenAI于2026年9月16日公布 Sponsored Agents，当前为美国部分广告主测试；9月23日公布的是 ChatGPT Ads 向东南亚六国及台湾扩展，不等同于 Sponsored Agents 已在这些市场全面开放。文中的一休、三慢问道与虾子曰场景为设计推演。

en.label: FIELD NOTES
en.title: The Best Ad May No Longer Be an Image, but a Salesperson You Can Talk To
en.excerpt: When an ad can understand space, budget, preferences, and doubts, the opportunity is to turn product knowledge into an honest conversation.
en.content:
![The Best Ad May No Longer Be an Image, but a Salesperson You Can Talk To](/assets/notes/2026-09-24-conversational-ads/cover.png)

Suppose you are about to buy a chair.

The ad tells you: **limited-time offer, design award winner, save 300 yuan today.**

But what you actually want to ask is: “My home is only 30 square meters—will it be too large?” “I have a cat—is the fabric easy to clean?” “My back hurts—will it become uncomfortable after a long time?” “The doorway is only 75 centimeters wide—will it fit through?”

An image cannot answer those questions. A landing page may run for dozens of screens, but you may not want to dig through it.

Now imagine someone beside the ad who knows the product, never pressures you, and is even willing to say, “This model is not right for you.” That changes the experience.

This is what interested me most about **Sponsored Agents**. They may change less about what an ad looks like than about the fact that an ad can finally listen to a person’s whole question.

![Advertising is changing from a poster into a conversation that understands real questions](/assets/notes/2026-09-24-conversational-ads/shift.png)

## 01｜For the First Time, an Ad Can Become a Conversation

On September 16, OpenAI announced new ChatGPT Ads capabilities, including Sponsored Agents in testing.

After seeing a clearly labeled ad, a user can choose to enter a conversation with the brand’s agent. They can ask about their space, budget, preferences, and concerns, understand whether the product actually fits, and then decide whether to visit the brand’s site.

OpenAI used a dining table as its example. Seeing the table is only the beginning. People will also ask how many it seats, whether it fits their dining room, and how it should be maintained.

Ads used to send people to a page, and the page tried to present everything at once. Now another layer appears between them: **first understand this person’s real problem.**

On September 23, ChatGPT Ads also began expanding to Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, Vietnam, and Taiwan. OpenAI said it had reached more than 60 countries and regions.

That does not mean Sponsored Agents are open in every market. They were still being tested with selected advertisers in the United States. But the direction is clear:

> **Advertising is moving from “look at me” to “what would you like to know?”**

## 02｜A Good Salesperson Is Better at Judging, Not Merely Talking

Traditional advertising is built to answer one question: **“Why should you buy me?”**

Conversational advertising must answer a harder one: **“In your specific situation, am I actually right for you?”**

The sentences are close, but their logic is very different. The first amplifies advantages; the second must understand limitations. The first pursues a click; the second needs trust.

A useful brand agent cannot merely recite marketing copy. It needs to know dimensions, price, materials, delivery times, and support boundaries. It must also know which needs the product cannot solve.

Sometimes its most valuable sentence may be: **“If this is what matters most to you, I would not recommend this model.”**

That may lose an order in the short term. In the long term, it may be the first time a user believes the thing on the other side of the screen is not trying only to close a sale.

## 03｜Landing Pages Will Remain, but Their Job Changes

Conversational ads naturally raise a question: will brands no longer need websites, product pages, or design?

My judgment is the opposite.

When AI summarizes a product for a user, the brand’s own content becomes evidence for its answer. Vague specifications, invented cases, and contradictory pages will only be exposed faster.

The layers will have clearer roles:

- **Ads create the meeting:** they appear when a need emerges.
- **Conversation supports judgment:** it discovers the context, concerns, and limits.
- **The website supplies proof:** it shows real cases, details, prices, and the brand’s attitude.
- **The app delivers experience:** it makes the promise happen and builds a lasting relationship.
- **The product fulfills the claim:** the product itself must still create the final value.

AI does not make brands unimportant. It makes vague brands harder to hide and serious products easier to understand.

## 04｜What This Could Mean for My Own Products

Imagine someone sees Yixiu described as “helping you relax,” then asks: “I often wake at three in the morning. I do not want a voice—only ten minutes of nature sounds. Is there something suitable?”

A good answer should not exaggerate medical effects. It can explain what Yixiu does and does not provide, then recommend Morning Forest Birds or another track based on time and sound preference, with a preview first.

For Wendao, someone may ask: “I feel stuck at work. What perspective can the Tao Te Ching offer?” The agent does not need to pretend it can make the decision. It can introduce a reading path from the original text and explanation to personal insight and everyday practice, then let the person decide whether this is how they want to read each day.

For Xiazi, a person may say: “I work in cross-border commerce. I only want yesterday’s important changes in AI and consumer brands, with links to the English sources.” The conversation should not repeat all 18 posters. It should help them find the part that matters to their work.

These are product-design exercises, not claims that these ads or agents are already live. But they clarify something for me:

> **Product communication should not only say what I have. It should help a person decide what it has to do with them.**

![A one-person company can turn real product knowledge into a sales capability that keeps answering questions](/assets/notes/2026-09-24-conversational-ads/knowledge.png)

## 05｜An Undervalued Opportunity for One-Person Companies

In the past, only large companies could afford presales teams that covered multiple time zones, knew the entire product line, and spoke several languages. A one-person company usually wrote an FAQ and hoped people would read it.

Conversational sales creates another possibility:

- questions asked at three in the morning can receive answers grounded in real material;
- one product can be explained in different languages to different markets;
- questions people would never send in a private message may finally be heard;
- every question teaches the creator what users are actually hesitating over.

There is no magic in which “connecting AI” automatically creates sales. An AI salesperson’s ceiling depends on the product facts you give it; its floor depends on whether you are willing to admit the product’s boundaries.

What a one-person company needs is not smoother sales talk but a maintainable **product knowledge base**: real specifications, use cases, who it suits, who it does not, common questions, comparison criteria, delivery processes, and support rules.

## 06｜Five Things You Can Do Now

1. **Collect 30 real questions.** Use messages, comments, support conversations, and trials with friends. Do not invent them at a desk.
2. **Write a page called “Who this is not for.”** A product willing to reject the wrong order is more likely to earn the right user’s trust.
3. **Put proof on your own website.** Cases, prices, specifications, and update history should be findable and citable.
4. **Become clear in your first language before translating.** AI can translate words; it cannot repair a vague position.
5. **Record questions, not only clicks.** What people repeatedly ask often reveals the product’s next improvement.

## 07｜Advertising Is Still a Mirror

I have never liked ads that chase people around. They know what I clicked, but not why I hesitated. They keep urging me to buy without asking whether the thing suits me.

Conversational advertising offers another possibility: when a user chooses, a brand can answer one specific question seriously instead of occupying a few seconds of attention.

It will also magnify bad products faster. If the product has no value, the agent is merely a more diligent promoter. If the facts are false, it will say the wrong thing more fluently.

The next generation of advertising may compete less on whose model is smarter and more on **who understands their product, who respects the user’s question, and who will trade one honest answer for a longer relationship.**

The best ad may truly stop being an image. It may feel like a knowledgeable, measured person who does not follow you around asking for an order—yet happens to be there when you need them.

---

Fact note: OpenAI announced Sponsored Agents on September 16, 2026, as a test for selected U.S. advertisers. Its September 23 announcement concerned expansion of ChatGPT Ads to six Southeast Asian countries and Taiwan; it did not mean Sponsored Agents were fully available in those markets. The Yixiu, Wendao, and Xiazi examples are design explorations.
